title: Foxbridge inference cost concordance and action list
body:
Purpose:
Quick internal brief reconciling Foxbridge's reported inference spend (billing export) with our Redwood Optimize modeled run-rate, and an actionable list of recommendations and implementation steps. This is a working doc intended for the Foxbridge AE + solutions handoff; contains conservative savings estimates and risk notes.

Executive snapshot (TL;DR):
- Customer: Foxbridge (B2B SaaS, heavy document summarization). Current avg monthly tokens: 1.6B; peak daily q1 traffic pattern.
- Current environment baseline (customer report): mix of hosted API + Dedicated small pool; running two model profiles for prod: base-gen-13b (standard fp16) and short-gen-6b for short prompts.
- Redwood Optimize recommended bundle: prefix KV caching + route-to-short-model for <75 tokens + 4-bit quantization on base-gen-13b + 120ms batching window for background jobs.
- Modeled gross token cost reduction: 43% (before SLAs & fallback overhead). Net expected run-rate improvement after rollout and conservative risk buffer: 28% YoY run-rate savings.

Baseline reconciliation (what we checked):
- Ingress: used Foxbridge billing CSV (Jan-Dec 2024) + usage export from hosted endpoints. Notable mismatch: billing counts include user-side client retries; we applied a 6% retry normalization (derived from logs).
- Latency SLOs: customer target p95 <= 400ms for interactive routes, batch jobs have 5s budget. We assume can apply batching only to non-interactive jobs.
- Models and weights: verified model parameters and compatibility with 4-bit quantization via runtime testbed (results attached in linked PR).

Assumptions used in the model:
- Token mix (prompt:completion) = 30:70 average for doc summarization.
- Short prompt threshold set at 75 tokens (empirically covers 62% of requests).
- Effective quantization multiplier: 0.45x GPU $/token for 4-bit relative to fp16 (includes inference efficiency + slightly lower throughput due to kernel maturity).
- Prefix caching reduces repeated-token compute by ~32% on their main summarization route.
- Implementation rollout cost accounted as 6 weeks eng time (SE + Solutions) and a phased canary with 5% -> 25% -> 60% traffic splits.

Detailed recommendations (by priority):
1) Quick win (0–3 weeks): route-to-short-model for requests with prompt+expected completion <75 tokens. Impact: immediate per-token unit-cost drop for ~62% traffic. Owner: Solutions Eng (Maya).
2) Medium (3–8 weeks): enable prefix/KV caching for the summarization route. Needs prompt normalization and deterministic cache keys; expected reduction of repeated decoding ~32%. Owner: Eng - Serving Runtime (Liam).
3) Medium (4–10 weeks): deploy base-gen-13b 4-bit quantized variant in Dedicated pool for Foxbridge (A/B test for quality). Run eval set of 500 prompts; monitor rouge/semantic delta. Owner: Applied ML (Carlos).
4) Low (6–12 weeks): apply 120ms batching window for nightly aggregation jobs; increases P50 latency but within 5s budget, huge throughput gains. Owner: Platform Eng.
5) Ongoing: tune autoscale/burst to minimize dedicated idle overhead; reserved capacity commit recommended only after stable 30% savings realized. Owner: Customer Success + Sales.

Modeled before/after (conservative):
- Before: $38,400/mo (normalized)
- After (gross): $21,900/mo (applying quantization + caching + routing)
- Implementation & quality buffer: +$1,400/mo (fallback/overhead amortized)
- After (net conservative): $23,300/mo => ~39% absolute dollar reduction (~28% run-rate after accounting for pricing/commits).

Quality & regression guardrails:
- Minimum pass criteria on evals: average semantic-similarity >= 0.94 vs fp16 baseline and no >2% failure cases for hallucination-sensitive prompts.
- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 3 days, review error/latency/quality dashboards, then 25% for 5 days, then 60% for 7 days. Automated rollback if quality delta > threshold.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quantization quality drift: mitigation = small-scale A/B with human review and automated evals; keep fp16 fallback route.
- Cache key collisions: mitigation = standardized prompt cleaning and versioned cache namespace.
- Billing discrepancies after rollout: maintain synchronized logging (request_id) and reconcile weekly; build a quick lookup in the spreadsheet (tab: reconciliation).

Next steps / action items (concrete):
- [Priya] Package a pull request with the quantized model artifact + inference config (due 2025-03-10).
- [Maya] Implement short-route detection rules in the API gateway and add tests (due 2025-03-07).
- [Liam] Prepare KV cache POC and cost/latency bench (due 2025-03-14).
- [CS/Sales] Draft a one-page customer-facing recommendation with estimated timeline and potential SLA notes (due 2025-03-12).

Spreadsheet pointers (internal):
- Cost model file: Foxbridge_CostModel_v3.xlsx (tab names: inputs, reconciliation, scenario_4bit_cache, rollout_timeline). See linked_artifacts.
- Key cells: inputs!B5 (token_rate), inputs!C8 (baseline_unit_cost), scenario_4bit_cache!D12 (modeled_net_savings).

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc attempts to stay conservative; I intentionally left buffer for fallback overheads. If Applied ML signs off on quality metrics we can tighten the net savings projection.
- Please annotate gaps you want filled (especially around autoscale economics for dedicated pool).

End of brief.
summary: Working brief reconciling Foxbridge billing with Redwood Optimize model and a prioritized action list. Conservative net run-rate savings estimate: ~28% after rollout and buffers.
